text: . Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff.Earlier, India’s three armed services – Army, Navy and the Air Force – planned, trained, procured and advised the government separately. Proposals for greater jointness had been made repeatedly since the Kargil Review Committee of 1999 and the Group of Ministers that followed it, but no single officer held authority across all three services. On the 15th of August 2019, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in his Independence Day address, announced the creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff from the ramparts of the Red Fort. Prime Minister Modi said this will lead to better coordination among the three services.The Cabinet approved the decision in December 2019, along with a new Department of Military Affairs within the Ministry of Defence for the CDS to head.  Talking to Akashvani News, retired Lt General Sanjay Kulkarni said the appointment of CDS made it possible for the government to have one point of contact for advice on allmiltarymatters.After the formation of the post of CDS, all three forces have now got effective leadership at the top level.

. In Uttar Pradesh, heavy and incessant rain has thrown life out of gear in many districts. Schools up to Class 12 will remain closed in several districts due to the heavy rain alert. Many districts, including state capital Lucknow, have been witnessing heavy rain due to cyclonic conditions over the last 24 hours. Normal life has been badly disrupted, and road traffic has also been affected due to heavy rain. Many rain-related accidents have also been reported from different parts of the state.Relief Commissioner of the state, Dr Hrishikesh Bhaskar Yashod, held a video conference with the District Magistrates of districts under red and orange alerts to review the weather situation and preparedness. He directed officials to remain active in the field, continuously monitor local conditions and ensure immediate action in any emergency situation.According to the India Meteorological Department forecast, weather conditions are likely to remain affected in the state on Saturday and Sunday. In eastern Uttar Pradesh, a warning of very heavy rainfall has been issued, along with heavy rainfall, thunder and lightning, and strong winds. In western Uttar Pradesh as well, heavy rainfall, thunder and lightning are likely till September 27.

. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar has raised concerns over repeated attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers in the Gulf, Red Sea and Black Sea, saying that the attacks were no longer exceptional occurrences. Dr Jaishankar was addressing the inaugural meeting of the ‘Group of Friends on Safety and Security of Shipping and Seafarers’ during the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.The External Affairs Minister announced a new initiative by India and Liberia together to draw greater attention to the safety and security of ships and seafarers. He said India, a major source of seafarers, and Liberia, the world’s largest shipping registry, have joined hands to strengthen maritime safety and security. The initiative aims to establish a consultative framework to enhance maritime security and ensure that key stakeholders have a greater voice in discussions on the sector.He pointed to the recent attack on the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged bulk carrier MV Cape Dao in the Gulf of Oman, which left an Indian sailor dead. Dr Jaishankar also mentioned the case of the Panama-flagged oil tanker El Gaia, which was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz and led to an Indian crew member being reported missing. The External Affairs Minister also drew attention to attacks on civilian ships in the Black Sea, including those involving MV Omorfi and MV Golden Leo.He said these incidents could no longer be viewed as isolated cases, as commercial ships and sailors have faced a series of attacks across key waterways. He said the attacks on commercial shipping had affected people from several countries, with seafarers of different nationalities also among those killed or affected. Dr Jaishankar said attacks that disrupt maritime trade and claim civilian lives could not be defended, and called on countries to work together to stop such incidents.The External Affairs Minister is in New York, leading the Indian delegation for the High-Level Week at the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly. Dr Jaishankar will address the High-Level Session today. During the visit, the Minister has attended various plurilateral and bilateral meetings.

. The second edition of the India Art, Architecture and Design Biennale (IAADB) will be held from 4th December 2026 to 21st March 2027 in New Delhi.The theme of this 108-day Biennale is ‘Tat Tvam Asi – Reconnecting in an Age of Distraction’. Talking exclusively to Akashvani News, Secretary of the Ministry of Culture, Vivek Aggarwal said that, the Biennale will feature art installations at iconic heritage sites of the National Capital, including Purana Qila, Red Fort, Safdarjung Tomb, Qutub Minar, Qila Rai Pithora and Lodhi Garden. He said that the theme of this year’s Biennale directly takes inspiration from India’s ancient traditions and spiritual thought, which emphasize self-introspection and the unity of the individual with the larger universal consciousness.Mr Aggarwal said that the Ministry aims to take IAADB to a global level by encouraging participation from international pavilions and artists, Indian states and the private sector.Speaking about the cultural diplomacy of India, He said that cultural exchange is an important component of cultural diplomacy and the country’s soft power. Mr Aggarwal added that participation of foreign countries will provide an opportunity for Indian and international audiences to experience diverse art forms and will help position the Biennale on the global cultural calendar.Underlining the importance of Art and Design students in this Biennale, He said that the Ministry plans to involve students, particularly those pursuing art and design, in various activities associated with the Biennale, providing them opportunities to engage with artists and the wider creative ecosystem.The second edition of the India Art, Architecture & Design Biennale 2026 is the largest platform which offers artists, curators, galleries, corporates, architects, designers, cultural institutions and other stakeholders a chance to connect with culture and the creative world. This edition is conceived not as a single exhibition in a single location but as a city-wide cultural platform. Visitors will have an opportunity to experience the historical monuments along with contemporary art installations.

. The Ministry of Education, in coordination with the External Affairs Ministry is organizing a two day Bharat Innovates Exposition from today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi to showcase India’s Deep-Tech innovations as a lead up to and alongside the 18th BRICS Summit 2026. The Exposition is showcasing 37 India’s Deep-Tech startups and ventures alligning with the theme of India’s BRICS Chairship Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. The event is providing participating innovators an opportunity to network with CEOs, investors, business leaders and industry representatives from BRICS member countries. Ministry of Eduaction said that the event will facilitate opportunities for Business to Business engagements, technology partnerships, investment discussions, business linkages and international market access.

. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar has said, frustration is growing within the international community over the lack of progress on reforming the United Nations. Dr Jaishankar was speaking at a ministerial session titled ‘Ruptures & Ramparts: Building Bridges for a Changing World’ on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly in New York. The External Affairs Minister said there is a growing feeling that the UN must change and better reflect the realities of the world today. He said countries opposing UN reforms cannot continue to use the organisation without supporting efforts to strengthen it.Dr Jaishankar also rejected the idea that UN reform can be achieved through unanimity. Drawing a parallel with democratic decision-making, he said countries should be free to put forward their views, after which decisions should be taken through voting. He said this is essential for moving the reform process forward. He stressed that meaningful reform requires a concrete text that can be negotiated. The External Affairs Minister also said there is greater willingness among countries of the Global South to work together on the issue. He said, countries are increasingly willing to engage with one another and work together, which is a positive development as it helps break old dependencies and contributes to a more democratic and balanced world.His remarks come as UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has called for reform of the Security Council, saying it must better reflect today’s world and have greater legitimacy to address current geopolitical challenges. India has long advocated reform of the Security Council, including expansion of both its permanent and non-permanent membership. New Delhi has argued that the 15-member Council, created in 1945, does not adequately reflect contemporary geopolitical realities.

The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) has released the 52nd monthly report on the Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System of Central Ministries and Departments’ performance for the month of August.More than 2.42 lakh grievances were redressed by central ministries and departments in August this year, with an average grievance disposal time taken of 13 days. The report states that the Department of Posts, the Department of Telecommunications and the Department of Financial Services (Insurance Division) topped the Group ‘A’ category in the rankings, while the Ministry of Steel, Shipping and the Ministry of Development of Northeastern topped the Group ‘B’ category.Over 1.38 lakh new users were registered last month, with the maximum registrations from West Bengal. The report provides a detailed analysis of types and categories of public grievances and the nature of disposal. The department also released the 49th report of CPGRAMS for states and union territories for the month of August. The department added that more than 98 thousand cases were received, and over 79 thousand grievances were redressed by the states and UTs last month.

In Ladakh, RNU Akashvani Kargil has launched a special podcast series under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, with the first programme focusing on “Natural Farming – Towards Sustainable and Climate-Resilient Agriculture.”The programme featured Dr. Nazir Hussain, Scientist, Krishi Vigyan Kendra Kargil, in conversation with Anayat Ali of RNU Akashvani Kargil.During the podcast, Dr. Nazir Hussain explained the principles of natural farming and highlighted its role in improving soil health, reducing dependence on external chemical inputs and promoting sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture.He discussed various aspects of the National Mission on Natural Farming, including chemical-free cultivation, livestock integration, diversified cropping, use of locally available bio-inputs and integration of traditional agricultural knowledge with scientific practices.Dr. Hussain said natural farming has considerable potential in Ladakh and Kargil, where agriculture is characterised by a short growing season, cold climatic conditions and limited water availability. He stressed the need for locally adapted practices, scientific research, farmer training and awareness for its successful adoption in the region.Comparing natural farming with organic farming, Dr. Hussain said natural farming can be more effective and efficient in boosting production while reducing farmers’ dependence on externally purchased inputs.The discussion also covered crop productivity, input costs, farmers’ income, water management, climate resilience and the need to make the transition towards natural farming economically viable for farmers.The special podcast series, produced by RNU Akashvani Kargil under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, will be broadcast daily at 4:30 PM from Akashvani Kargil. The programmes will also be available on the AIRNews Kargil YouTube channel.

. The nation today is paying homage to Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, a towering figure of India’s social reform movement, on his 207th birth anniversary. Born on 26 September 1820 at Birsingha in Paschim Medinipur district in West Bengal, Vidyasagar dedicated his life to education and social reform. He was a strong advocate of women’s education and played a historic role in the campaign for Hindu widow remarriage, which led to the enactment of the Hindu Widows’ Remarriage Act in 1856.He also worked against child marriage and polygamy and promoted education among girls by helping establish schools for them. As an educationist, he played a major role in modernising education and simplifying Bengali prose. His Barnaparichay became a landmark primer for Bengali children.It may be said that social reformer Raja Rammohan Roy helped open the door to social and intellectual reform; Vidyasagar pushed that reform deeper into society, especially in the lives of women and children.

A coalition of 22 US attorneys general has opposed the Trump administration’s proposal to impose a fee exceeding 100,000 dollars on certain H-1B visa petitions, arguing that the measure is unlawful and would worsen shortages of teachers, doctors and nurses. The challenge is significant for Indian professionals and American companies that rely heavily on the H-1B programme to recruit highly skilled workers. The proposed charge could make it more difficult for state and local institutions to recruit skilled foreign professionals, the attorneys general said. They cited shortages in primary and secondary education, healthcare and other essential services.Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones joined the coalition in filing a formal comment letter asking US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) to withdraw the proposed rule. Besides Virginia, the coalition includes the attorneys general of California, Massachusetts, Arizona, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Hawaii, Illinois, Maine, Maryland, Michigan and Minnesota. It also includes Nevada, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, North Carolina, Oregon, Washington, Wisconsin and the District of Columbia.According to the attorneys general, the administration has failed to justify the burden that the proposed charge would impose on states. They also said USCIS had not adequately considered less damaging alternatives. They argued that the executive branch cannot impose such a tax without authorisation from Congress.The agency issued the notice of proposed rulemaking on August 25. It would impose a charge of 103,265 dollars on petitions filed by employers that are not exempt from the annual H-1B visa cap. The H-1B programme allows US employers to hire foreign workers in specialty occupations that generally require specialised knowledge and at least a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent.

. Defending champions India held Azerbaijan to a 2-2 draw in the eighth round of the FIDE Chess Olympiad in Samarkand yesterday. R Praggnanandhaa, Arjun Erigaisi, D Gukesh and Vidit Santosh Gujrathi were all held to draws by their Azerbaijani opponents.Gukesh drew with Muradli Mahammad after 56 moves, while Praggnanandhaa drew with Shakhriyar Mamedyarov, Arjun with Aydin Suleymanli and Vidit with Rauf Mamedov. India remained in joint second place in the Open section with 13 match points. Uzbekistan and Germany share the lead with 14 match points after Germany defeated the hosts 2.5-1.5.In the women’s section, defending champions India drew 2-2 with Kazakhstan and remained in joint second place. B Savitha Shri secured her seventh consecutive victory by defeating Elnaz Kaliakhmet. Koneru Humpy and Divya Deshmukh drew, while Vaishali Rameshbabu lost to Nurman Alua..

. Vice-President CP Radhakrishnan has congratulated Kamaljeet and Suruchi Inder Singh on winning the Gold Medal in the 10m Air Pistol Mixed Team event at the Asian Games 2026. In a social media post, the Vice-President said that their exceptional precision and partnership have brought glory to the nation.Mr Radhakrishnan also congratulated M R Poovamma, Vithya Ramraj, Manu T S and Vishal T K on securing the Silver Medal in the 4x400m Mixed Relay in the Games. He also congratulated Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar, Rudrankksh Balasaheb Patil and Niraj Kumar on winning Silver in the Men’s 50m Rifle 3 Positions Team event. The Vice-President said that their remarkable performances and teamwork have added to India’s growing medal tally. He also wished them continued success.

. India has welcomed the commencement of the QUAD-at-Sea Ship Observer Mission, announced at the 11th Quad Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in New Delhi on 26th of May this year. The External Affairs Ministry said in a social media post that India Coast Guard ship Shaunak has sailed from Chennai with sea riders from all four Quad countries. It said the mission strengthens maritime cooperation and interoperability, reflecting the Quad’s shared commitment to a free and open Indo-Pacific.Meanwhile, the Defence Ministry said in a statement that this marks an important step in advancing maritime cooperation and interoperability among QUAD nations – India, Australia, Japan, and the United States. Six Sea Riders – two officers each from India and Japan, and one officer each from Australia and the United States – embarked onboard Shaunak to participate in shipboard activities and professional exchanges.

External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar met his counterparts from Iran and Russia, discussing a range of bilateral issues, cooperation in the BRICS grouping and the Gulf conflict.Mr Jaishankar said that he met Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly in New York and discussed bilateral issues as well as a number of ongoing issues. Mr Jaishankar also met Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on the margins of the high-level UNGA session. They discussed the latest developments with regard to the Gulf conflict.Referring to the grouping of Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa and the United Arab Emirates, Jaishankar said the leaders of the grouping took stock of BRICS cooperation.India earlier this month hosted the BRICS Leaders’ Summit, which was attended by Russian President Vladimir Putin and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian.

Artificial intelligence could increase aggregate labour productivity by as much as 3.8% over the long term, according to a new International Monetary Fund (IMF) working paper that examined patent and employment data across developed economies. The study found that the rapid expansion of AI-related innovation had already produced measurable productivity gains. It estimated that AI patent activity between 2000 and 2017 increased output per worker by between 0.8% and 1.2%.The findings were published yesterday in an IMF working paper titled “Artificial Intelligence and Aggregate Labor Productivity: Evidence from Patent Data.” The researchers examined the aggregate effect of AI technology on labour productivity using patent data from countries belonging to the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development. The study covered the period between 2000 and 2017.The findings suggest that AI may generate stronger economic returns when it complements the work performed by skilled employees rather than merely replacing existing tasks.

. The Ministry of Corporate Affairs has issued an advisory to the common public about ‘Nidhi Companies’ and their functioning. The Ministry has warned against investment decisions without a proper background check, especially if there is a promise of high returns.The Nidhi companies are mutual-benefit companies regulated by the Corporate Affairs Ministry under the Companies Act, 2013 and Nidhi Rules, 2014, which can accept deposits and give loans only to their members.The Ministry said that during examination of NDH-4 applications, it was noticed that many ‘Nidhi’ Companies are not complying with the applicable provisions of the Act and rules made there under in toto.The Ministry informed that the deposits accepted by Nidhi Companies are not insured by the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation.  It added that if the company fails or faces fraud, recovery of deposited money can be very difficult or incomplete.

In the FIDE Chess Olympiad, reigning World Classical Chess Champion Dommaraju Gukesh secured a clutch win to help India beat overnight joint-topper Germany 2.5-1.5 in the ninth round of the men’s Open section, moving up to second position in the standings.With this win, India roared back into title contention as they are in a good position to challenge table-toppers Uzbekistan for the title. In the crucial clash on Table 2, R. Praggnanandhaa, Arjun Erigaisi and Nihal Sarin were held to draws on the first three boards before Gukesh secured the lone victory of the match against Germany.In the women’s section, B Savitha Shri’s incredible run of seven successive wins came to an end, but she remained unbeaten after a draw against Karimova Guldona of Uzbekistan on the top table. Koneru Humpy was held by top Uzbek Afruza Khamdamova, but Women’s World Cup winner Divya Deshmukh and Ventika Agrawal won their games to secure a 3-1 win for India.The victory took them to 15 points from nine rounds as they shared the second spot with Kazakhstan and Mongolia. Armenia went down 1-3 to leaders China, while Mongolia drew 2-2 with Kazakhstan.

Chinese President Xi Jinping wrapped up a three-day state visit to Washington with progress on trade, discussions on artificial intelligence and foreign policy, but with no major new agreements between the world’s two largest economies.President Donald Trump said they had a really great meeting, great for everybody, great for the farmers, great for everybody. Chinese President Xi Jinping said he will meet President Donald Trump two more times before the end of the year, doubling the number of face-to-face discussions between the leaders of the world’s two largest economies in 2026.The most concrete outcome came on trade, where the United States and China agreed to extend their current trade truce for another two months. The extension keeps the truce in place into January while negotiations continue. U.S. tariffs on Chinese goods had climbed as high as 145%, while China tightened restrictions on exports of rare-earth materials critical to electronics, advanced manufacturing and other high-tech products.Artificial intelligence was another major topic during the visit, and no major new AI agreement was announced. Xi said the United States and China share a responsibility to work together on the technology and ensure it remains under human control. The United States has also proposed creating a mechanism through which the two countries could alert one another about dangerous AI incidents with national security implications.Foreign policy discussions included the ongoing war with Iran. Trump said he and Xi discussed the conflict, but no breakthrough was announced. Taiwan also remains one of the most sensitive sources of tension between Washington and Beijing. Despite those unresolved issues, Trump repeatedly emphasised his personal relationship with Xi, describing it as a truly great friendship.Some trade analysts say few tangible accomplishments seemed to have come from the meeting. Little was announced outside of the promise of more meetings between Washington and Beijing. The three-day state visit by Xi has been criticised by some in the U.S. for being heavy on pomp and light on substance.

Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Punya Salila Srivastava, reaffirmed India’s commitment to strengthening global pandemic preparedness and response at the UN High-Level Meeting in New York. Addressing the meeting, the Secretary outlined India’s coordinated approach to pandemic prevention and response across government and society, which covers a wide range of potential health emergencies. She underlined the efforts taken by India to expand laboratory networks, emergency coordination, health workforce, stockpiles and clinical care capacity to ensure that systems are equipped to respond effectively to health emergencies. Ms Srivastava stressed the need to translate the lessons of the COVID-19 pandemic into sustained investment, institutional capacity and resilient health systems.She also underscored the importance of solidarity and fair access to essential health products. She said that during the COVID-19 pandemic, India supplied 300 million vaccine doses to around 100 countries and two UN entities, while providing medical assistance to over 150 countries. Ms Srivastava said this reflected India’s commitment to the principle of One Earth, One Health.Speaking on the occasion, WHO Director-General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called for urgent action to strengthen global pandemic preparedness.

. Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh has said that critical minerals are key to India’s energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. The Minister said this while addressing a special plenary of the 3rd Global Summit on Advanced Materials, Critical Minerals, and Metals in New Delhi. Dr Singh said that critical minerals and metals will be a driving component of the next phase of technological development, with their importance extending beyond mining to energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. He said that the global economy is undergoing a paradigm shift, with clean energy, electric mobility, semiconductors, telecommunications, aerospace, defence and nuclear energy emerging as major drivers of technological and industrial transformation. He added, India is now participating in this global discourse with much greater confidence and is preparing to assume a larger global role.Dr. Singh has called for early industry linkage with research and innovation, saying potential industry partners should be brought on board right from the beginning. He further said that a healthy synergy among research, industry, government and the non-government sector is essential for sustaining startups and entrepreneurs. The Minister also highlighted on building domestic capabilities for energy security as the world moves towards cleaner and greener sources of energy. He said that India’s next phase of growth in strategic technologies and materials will depend on working together of all stakeholders.

. The International Centre for Automotive Technology (ICAT), Manesar, today celebrated its 20 years of service to India’s automotive industry. Heavy Industries Minister HD Kumaraswamy and Minister of State for Heavy Industries, Bhupathi Raju Srinivasa Varma, were present on the occasion.  The event featured an industry dialogue on the PM e-Drive scheme, a flagship initiative envisioned under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi to accelerate India’s transition towards clean, sustainable, and self-reliant mobility. The event saw the inauguration of an indigenous Agri Machinery Test Facility, a first-of-its-kind initiative aimed at supporting farmers by ensuring reliable, certified equipment for agricultural modernization. During the event, it was emphasized that ICAT’s journey is not only about the past 20 years but also about the future, where India is poised to achieve global leadership in both automotive and agricultural technologies through innovation, dedication, and collaboration.

. Mizoram emerged champions in the North East Regional Muaythai Championship, with around 350 fighters from across the eight northeastern states competing in 100 categories. Meghalaya finished as first runner-up and Tripura second runner-up in the championship organised by the Mizoram Muaythai Association at R. Dengthuama Hall here.  Chief Minister Lalduhoma attended the closing ceremony and congratulated the participating fighters.Addressing the gathering, Lalduhoma said Muaythai had emerged as a prominent contact sport globally and, although it was yet to be included in the Olympics, had developed into a professional discipline capable of providing livelihood opportunities. He cited Mizo fighter Nazareth Lalthazuala, who has secured a contract with ONE Championship, as an example of opportunities available in the sport.The Chief Minister said contact sports are particularly suited to the youth of Mizoram and other northeastern states and urged young people to pursue their sporting talents with determination. He called upon the fighters to train harder and strive for excellence, saying sports could provide livelihoods as well as bring honour to the state and strengthen bonds among people in the region.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that over the past 12 years, the gap between cities and villages in India has narrowed significantly. He highlighted the considerable improvement in rural infrastructure and noted that women across the country have also become increasingly self-reliant and economically empowered.PM Modi made these remarks during a virtual interaction with Seva Yatris travelling on the Yatra from Varanasi to Vadnagar under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan. He emphasised the importance of social service, social reform and positive change. He said Viksit Bharat can be realised only with the contribution and participation of everyone.PM Modi highlighted that Vadnagar gave him the values that shaped his life, while Kashi added countless colours of service to those values. He expressed happiness that young people are also enriching this journey with the many colours of service.During the interaction, these yatris shared their experiences with the Prime Minister. PM Modi also urged the yatris to maintain a diary and record their experiences during the Yatra.

. Bangladesh has launched a special nationwide measles-rubella (MR) vaccination campaign targeting around 34 lakh unvaccinated or missed children aged six months to under five years. The campaign is being conducted by the Health and Family Welfare Ministry under the title ‘Intensified MR Catch-up Vaccination’ at the T&T playground and in various areas of Dhaka today.The campaign will continue until October 31 and aims to identify children who were missed during the ongoing MR vaccination campaign and arrange vaccination for them. Children who have reached six months of age during this period and have become newly eligible will also be covered.Health workers and volunteers will conduct house-to-house visits to verify children’s vaccination status and identify children who are outside existing vaccination lists or previous campaign data.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended on a positive note today. The Sensex rose 315 points to close at 73,896. The Nifty gained 77 points to settle at 23,141. The broader market at the National Stock Exchangedisplayed mixedtrend. The Midcap 100 index dropped over 0.1 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index rose more than 0.1 per cent.In the forex market, the rupee appreciated by 14 paise to trade at 95 rupees and 82 paise against the US dollar.In the global crude oil market, Brent Crude was trading one per cent down at 105 US dollars and five cents per barrel, while WTI Crude was trading 1.7 per cent lower at 92 US dollars and 99 cents per barrel in intra-day trade.At the Multi Commodity Exchange, Gold for the October contract was trading 0.7 per cent up at 1,51,709 rupees per 10 grams, and Silver for the December contract was trading 1.3 per cent higher at 2,36,574 rupees per kilogram, when reports last came in.For more updates about the market activities, tune in to Akashvani’s bilingual programme ‘Market Mantra’ at 6:30 PM this evening.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall with isolated extremely heavy rainfall over Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand tomorrow. According to IMD, heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely over Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh tomorrow. The districts that are likely to receive heavy rainfall include Rampur, Pilibhit, Bareilly, Shahjahanpur and Bahraich. Meanwhile, districts of Madhya Pradesh which are expected to receive rainfall include Satna, Chhatarpur, Tikamgarh and Niwari.IMD said that the line of withdrawal of Southwest Monsoon continues to pass through Gurdaspur, Chandigarh, Muzaffarnagar, Aligarh, Dholpur, Udaipur, Deesa and Naliya.The Met Department has also predicted heavy rainfall over Delhi, Haryana, Chandigarh, Bihar, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim for the day. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty windsare expectedto prevail over Punjab, Madhya Pradesh, Vidarbha, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Mahe, Telangana, Andaman and Nicobar Islands and parts of Northeast during the next two days.Meanwhile, parts of Delhi are expected to witness light to moderate rainfall tomorrow.

The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) has proposed a major overhaul of the insurance distribution framework, including a simpler three-tier architecture, lower expense limits, revamped commission structures and stronger safeguards against mis-selling.The insurance regulator released a public consultation paper on “Recalibrating Economics of Insurance Distribution”, outlining reforms covering distribution structure, expenses, commissions, market conduct, transparency and the use of digital infrastructure.Under the proposed norms, insurers and large distribution entities will have to disclose their commission policies and structures in a simple and accessible manner. Specified commercial policies will also carry commission disclosures, enabling customers to be aware of the distribution costs built into the pricing. The consultation paper also proposes tighter measures to curb mis-selling and compulsory bundling of insurance with other financial products.These include documenting customer needs and suitability, bringing direct and indirect remuneration within the regulatory definition of commission, and prohibiting volume-linked or reward-linked incentives for bank and Non-Banking Financial Company staff selling insurance. IRDAI has further proposed linking the identity of the individual seller with each policy, placing information on mis-selling incidents in the public domain and allowing commission claw-backs in cases of mis-selling.A key part of the proposed reforms is a reduction in insurers’ Expense of Management (EoM) limits. For life insurers, the EoM limit would shift to a company-level basis linked to Gross Direct Premium Income (GDPI), with the ceiling proposed at 15 per cent within two years and 12.5 per cent within five years. For general insurers, the calculation would shift from Gross Written Premium (GWP) to domestic GDPI, while the EoM limit would progressively decline from 30 per cent of GWP to 20 per cent of GDPI within five years.

Indian squash players have assured themselves of three medals at the Asian Games, with Joshna Chinappa and Velavan Senthilkumar reaching the mixed doubles semifinals, while Anahat Singh and Abhay Singh entered the last four in singles.Joshna and Velavan defeated the Philippines’ David Pelino and Jemyca Aribado 11-3, 11-5 in the mixed doubles quarterfinals. In women’s singles, Anahat Singh beat compatriot Tanvi Khanna 11-2, 11-5, 11-3, while Abhay Singh defeated Japan’s Ryonosuke Tsukue 11-4, 11-3, 11-6.Abhay will face Pakistan’s Irfan Muhammad in the semifinals after Muhammad defeated India’s Veer Chotrani. The men’s and women’s singles gold medallists at the Games will directly qualify for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, where squash will make its Olympic debut.

. Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh today said that the focus of wellness must shift to preventive healthcare and physical and mental well-being, rather than the mere absence of diseases. The Minister was speaking at the Health and Wellness Summit 2026 in New Delhi. Dr Singh said that over the last decade, India has increasingly moved towards a broader understanding of health, with greater emphasis on Ayurveda, Yoga and wellness centres alongside modern healthcare.He said that advances in healthcare and wider access to medical facilities have significantly improved the ability to diagnose and treat serious illnesses. Dr. Singh underlined that the Government has adopted a broader approach to healthcare, combining improved access to treatment with preventive and grassroots interventions.The Minister said that science and technology have an important role in addressing emerging health challenges, particularly by developing solutions that are affordable, accessible and suited to local needs. He said that continued collaboration among medical practitioners, researchers, industry and other stakeholders will be important in developing practical solutions for emerging health challenges. He said the objective should be to build a healthier India in which preventive healthcare and wellness become an integral part of the country’s journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047.

. The Centre has extended the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act, 1958, in ‘disturbed areas’ of Manipur, Nagaland and Arunachal Pradesh for a period of six months with effect from 1st of October.In Manipur, the Ministry of Home Affairs extended AFSPA in the entire state, excluding the areas falling under the jurisdiction of 13 Police stations.In Nagaland, AFSPA has been extended in nine districts. These districts are Dimapur, Niuland, Chumoukedima, Mon, Kiphire, Noklak, Phek, Peren and Meluri. In Arunachal Pradesh, AFSPA has been extended in Tirap, Changlang and Longding districts and the areas falling within the jurisdiction of Namsai, Mahadevpur and Chowkham police stations in Namsai district, bordering Assam.

. The Indian women’s kabaddi team clinched gold after beating Iran at the 2026 Asian Games. The Indian women went on an unbeaten run throughout their campaign. The dominant Indian side edged out Iran in a tense final clash at the Tokai Citizen Gymnasium in Aichi-Nagoya, winning the contest by a 37-34 margin.The gold medal triumph was India’s third of the ongoing Asiad competition, following the women’s cricket team and the shooting pair of Suruchi Singh Phogat and Kamaljeet in the 10m air pistol mixed team event on Friday.India’s men’s kabaddi team will also face Iran in the final later today, aiming to complete a golden double.The men had won seven straight Asian Games gold medals before their streak ended in 2018, but they reclaimed the title at the 2023 Hangzhou Games.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Bihar, East Madhya Pradesh, East Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and North Eastern parts of the country during the next two days. IMD said that thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are likely to prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Bihar, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. Meanwhile, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Mahe are expected to experience hot and humid weather till 8th of this month.

. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) today absorbed 75,026 crore rupees from the banking system through an overnight Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR) auction, amid surplus liquidity. The RBI absorbed the liquidity at a cut-off and weighted average rate of 5.24 per cent.According to RBI data, as on 22nd September, liquidity in the banking system was in surplus of 4.45 trillion rupees. The RBI has been conducting VRRR auctions to absorb excess liquidity and align overnight money market rates with the repo rate. The central bank has also conducted open market operations (OMO) sales of government securities worth 50,000 crore rupees on 17th September and 25,000 crore rupees on 21st September.The remaining 25,000 crore rupees tranche is scheduled for 28th September. The RBI had announced total OMO sales of one trillion rupees in three tranches to manage liquidity conditions.

. Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah has called for the creation of a Himalayan Climate Resilience Mechanism, jointly led by Nepal, India and China, following devastating flash floods in the Himalayan region. Addressing the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in his maiden speech last night, Prime Minister Shah warned that a warming climate is destabilising the fragile Himalayan ecosystem. He proposed using the mechanism to share satellite data, technical expertise and early-warning information among the three countries. He said melting permafrost is weakening mountain slopes beneath glaciers and increasing the risk of ice-rock avalanches, floods, landslides and other cascading disasters. He said the recent disaster caused widespread devastation on both sides of the Nepal-China border, with floodwaters continuing downstream into India.Mr Shah also expressed Nepal’s deep gratitude to countries, including India, that provided assistance following the disaster.Nepal was hit by massive flash floods on the 26th of last month, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border. The floods devastated towns and villages across northern and central Nepal. The disaster has claimed 1,452 lives, while between 4,700 and 6,000 people are still reported missing.

. Surgeons of the Armed Forces Medical Services (AFMS) carried out 220 sight-restoring surgeries during the 10th edition of first-of-its-kind Mega Eye Surgical Camp, held under Operation Drishti in Kupwara, Jammu and Kashmir. The operation was held on the 24th and 25th of this month.DefenceMinistry said that most interventions were cataract surgeries, along with selective retinal procedures and minimally invasive glaucoma surgery. Chief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth visited the camp and interacted with patients. The camp was ledby Headof Ophthalmology at Army Hospital (Research and Referral), Delhi Cantonment, Brigadier Sanjay Kumar Mishra.AFMS’ series of mega surgical eye camps have so far screened over 1.50 lakh patients. The Ministry said that over three thousand 500 surgeries have been conducted across 10 cities.

. In the Asian Games, India’s overall medal tally has reached 23, with 2 Gold, 9 Silver and 12 Bronze in Japan. Indian duo Kamaljeet and Suruchi Singh won gold in the mixed team 10m air pistol event in Nagoya, Japan, today. The pair shot 484.6 in the final to finish 6.6 points ahead of South Korea’s Suhyeon Hong and Gaeun Choo, who took silver with 478.Indian long-distance runner Gulveer Singh won the silver medal in the men’s 10,000m race at the Asian Games. Indian athlete Baranica Elangovan won the bronze medal in the women’s pole vault at the Asian Games. Another Indian athlete, Manpreet Kaur, won the bronze medal in the women’s shot put.In Table Tennis, Indian Mixed Doubles pair of Diya Chitale and Manush Shah settled for a bronze medal after losing to World Champions and Chinese combination Wang Chuqin and Sun Yingsha 0-3.India’s men’s and women’s kabaddi teams have also entered the finals at the Asian Games after registering comprehensive victories in their respective semifinal matches.Indian squash players have assured themselves of three medals at the Asian Games, with Joshna Chinappa and Velavan Senthilkumar reaching the mixed doubles semifinals, while Anahat Singh and Abhay Singh entered the last four in singles.

. Iran has offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume talks on its nuclear programme in seven days if the United States lifts its naval blockade of Iranian ports, waives sanctions on Iranian oil sales and observes a ceasefire that would include Lebanon.Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi detailed the proposal to reporters outside the UN Security Council, saying it would also restart stalled talks with the US on Iran’s nuclear programme. The seven-day timeline will start as soon as the United States accepts this plan, he said.Araghchi said initial steps would take about four to five days to complete, and the strait would be open on the sixth day. On day seven, talks with the US would begin for the final deal on mutually agreed subjects, he said, referring to the nuclear programme.The White House said that US officials are having positive and constructive conversations with mediators on the Iran war. There was no immediate comment on the proposal from Gulf Arab nations, although Saudi Arabia was sceptical of the latest push for a deal.Iran’s disruption of the strait — through which a fifth of the world’s traded oil and gas transited before the war — has emerged as its main point of leverage. The effects have been felt far beyond the Middle East and posed political problems for President Donald Trump and his Republican Party ahead of November’s midterm congressional elections.

. Today is World Suicide Prevention Day. The day is observed worldwide to raise awareness about suicide prevention and the importance of mental health.The occasion reminds us that people facing emotional distress or difficult circumstances need timely support, understanding and appropriate care. Experts emphasise that listening to someone with patience and without judgement can encourage them to seek help and support.On this Day, people are encouraged to remain attentive to the emotional well-being of those around them and, when required, guide them towards family members, trusted persons or mental health professionals.

. In the Asian Games, the Indian duo Kamaljeet and Suruchi Singh stormed into the final of the mixed team 10m air pistol event after topping the qualification with a strong performance today in Nagoya, Japan.After registering a 196 in the opening series, the Indian pair raced to 391 at the end of second series after scoring 195, placing them within sight of making the finals with just 20 shots remaining. They aggregated another 196 in the third series to take their tally to 587, which included 29 inner 10s. The top four pairs advance to the final. This is India’s final chance for a medal in the 10m air pistol events after a disappointing campaign so far.In table tennis mixed doubles, India’s Manush Shah and Diya Chitale stunned world No. 4 Doo Hoi Kem and Wong Chun Ting of Hong Kong 3-1 to reach the semi finals at the Asian Games. The Indian duo won 11-6, 13-15, 11-9, 11-5 in the quarterfinals to secure India’s first table tennis medal at the ongoing Games. Shah and Chitale will now face China’s Sun Yingsha and Wang Chuqin in the semifinals.

. The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) hasissued redalert for extremely heavy rainfall over isolated places of Chhattisgarh, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Telangana for the next two days. The Met Department has predicted heavy rainfall over Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Bihar, Jharkhand, Kerala, Maharashtra, West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. The weather department also forecast thunderstorms accompanied with highly gusty winds over Madhya Pradesh and Parts of North-East tomorrow.For Delhi, IMD said the national capital will witness mostly clear skies with no rain. The maximum temperature in Delhi is expected to be around 34 to 35 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature of 23 to 25 degrees Celsius.

. Indian athlete Baranica Elangovan won the bronze medal in the women’s pole vault at the Asian Games at Aichi-Nagoya in Japan today. Thismarks country’sfirst-ever medal in the pole vault event at the Asian Games. The 29-year-old athlete secured the podium finish with a best clearance of 4.15 metres.While her compatriot Sindhushree Ganesha exited the competition without registering a mark, Baranica stayed in strong contention, navigating the field as Japan’s Misaki Morota led the event.This achievement caps off a standout year for Baranica. Earlier this year, she shattered the National Record twice-first leaping 4.22m in March and later rewriting it to 4.23m in May at Bhubaneswar. With this, India’s overall medal tally has risen to 23,comprising, twogold, nine silver and twelve bronze.

. Reserve Bank of India Deputy Governor Rohit Jain today said technology was no longer merely an enabler of banking but was increasingly becoming part of banks’ risk architecture.Addressing the 13th SBI Banking & Economics Conclave 2026 in Mumbai, Mr Jain highlighted the growing role of technology in banking and said technology is now embedded in almost every critical banking function, from core banking and payments to customer onboarding, credit assessment, fraud monitoring, and even regulatory reporting.On artificial intelligence, Jain said it could improve customer service, fraud detection, risk assessment and productivity, but could also amplify errors and influence decisions related to credit, fraud alerts, customer access, pricing and service delivery.Mr Jain that boards and senior management must have sufficient technological understanding to question assumptions, assess dependencies and ensure that resilience arrangements are properly tested.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices rebounded today. The Sensex rose 299 points or 0.4 per cent to close at 74,828. The Nifty jumped 118 points or half a per cent to settle at 23,447.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index climbed 0.7 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index gained 0.9 per cent.

. Vultures are extremely important for our ecosystem. By feeding on dead animals, they help keep the environment clean and reduce the spread of harmful diseases.However, vulture populations have declined significantly because of habitat loss, poisoning, and certain veterinary medicines that are harmful to them. Conservation efforts are therefore essential to protect these birds and maintain the balance of nature.On this International Vulture Day, government and environmental experts have urged people to understand, protect, and conserve vultures for a healthier environment.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices slumped over 1.6 percent today. The Sensex tanked 1, 248 points to close at 73, 581 while the Nifty plunged 384 points to settle at 23,063.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index shed 2.3 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index lost over 1.5%.This morning, Markets opened with a gap-down as spike in bond yields, elevated crude oil prices and a sell-off in banking and insurance stocks weighed on the indices. The Sensex and Nifty remained under pressure throughout the session, with sell-off intensifying during the second half of the trade.In the Sensex pack, 29 out of 30 companies logged losses with NTPC remaining unchanged. Among the top under performers, Bajaj Finance lost 5.5%, Axis Bank declined 4.7 per cent and Bajaj Finserv fell 4.1 per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, all 28 sectors edged downward. Among the top losers, Mid-Small Private Banks declined 2.8 per cent, Housing Finance lost 2.6 per cent and Financial Services shed more than 2.3 per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 2,884 companies declined, 1,473 advanced and 216 remained unchanged.

. The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) facilitated the flag-off of a one MT consignment of GI-tagged Gulbarga Tur Dal from Karnataka to the Maldives. The consignment, exported yesterday by M/s Silken Global Exports and Imports, Mysuru, through its Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO)-led brand, will be transported to the Maldives by sea. The Ministry of Commerce and Industry said that the initiative is aimed at expanding international markets for India’s GI-tagged agricultural products and strengthening the participation of FPO-led brands in agri exports.It added that a key feature of the export-linked value chain is improved price realisation for farmers, which enables farmers to realise 82 rupees per kg against prevailing market price of 60 rupees per kg. It provides FPOs an opportunity to participate more closely in export-oriented value chains and connect producers with international markets. The Ministry further noted that the export is expected to pave the way for regular shipments of Gulbarga Tur Dal to the Maldives, creating sustained market opportunities for producers and exporters from Karnataka. The initiative is also expected to support greater value realisation for farmers and enable FPOs and farmers to integrate more closely with export-oriented value chains.

. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar co-chaired the India-Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) Troika Ministerial Meeting in New York on the sidelines of the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly. In a social media post, Dr Jaishankar said the meeting reviewed the progress of the India-GCC Joint Action Plan 2024-28 and discussed ways to further advance the partnership.He welcomed the launch of negotiations for the India-GCC Free Trade Agreement. He said India looks forward to strengthening ties with the GCC in areas including trade, investment, energy, food security, health, new technologies, culture and people-to-people exchanges. Dr Jaishankar also thanked the GCC leadership for its support to the Indian community. He reiterated India’s strong commitment to freedom of navigation and the safety of seafarers and commercial shipping.

. Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran has highlighted India’s ability to attract foreign capital with its broader manufacturing and overall reforms. Addressing the 13th PAFI annual forum in New Delhi, Mr Nageswaran emphasized that the most important thing for the industry is global competitiveness. He added that the global environment in which investment decisions are made has now shifted, making it important to assess India’s foreign direct investment performance in that context.Mr Nageswaran also pointed to investor protection, tax-policy certainty and consistency, and availability of skilled talent and logistics as other factors that can influence investment decisions. He noted that changing global interest-rate environments could also have a significant bearing on the cost of capital and cross-border investment flows.

. Chhattisgarh government has declared a holiday for all schools in the state today amid continuous rain over the past two days. Heavy rainfall has caused water levels in several rivers, including the Indravati, Mahanadi and Shivnath, to rise, while low-lying areas in several cities and towns are facing waterlogging.Heavy rain over the past three days has affected several districts, including the Bastar division and central parts of the state. In Bastar, the Indravati River is flowing seven feet above the danger mark. All gates of the Gangrel Dam in Dhamtari district have been opened, leading to a rapid rise in the water level of the Mahanadi River.The Shivnath River in Durg district is also in spate, resulting in flood-like conditions in several areas. People stranded in flood-affected areas, including Durg and Bastar, have been shifted to safer locations. Traffic has been affected on several roads, including the Raipur-Jagdalpur National Highway.Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai has directed collectors of the affected districts to remain fully alert and ensure relief and rescue operations.

. Indian marathon runner Sawan Barwal created history at the Asian Games 2026 by winning a silver medal in the men’s marathon event, ending India’s 44-year wait for a podium finish in the discipline. Barwal clocked 2:11:37 to register a personal best and set a new national record in the men’s marathon final. He finished behind Japan’s Yamashita, who claimed the gold medal after pulling ahead in the closing stages of the race.

. National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) Managing Director and CEO Dilip Asbe today said around 75 per cent of transaction volumes would fall outside the scope of the new merchant discount rate (MDR) regime, as 96 per cent of transactions are below 2,000 rupees.Addressing the SBI Banking and Economics Conclave in Mumbai, Asbe said there is “huge miscommunication and misinformation” surrounding the MDR regime and that NPCI and the government is trying to provide clear information.Mr Asbe clarified that the new regime will not hurt UPI volumes because most of the MDR will come from merchants who already accept credit cards and therefore, already pay MDR.
